text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is officially diagnosed when readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg according to guidelines from the American Heart Association and Mayo Clinic.
snippet_highlighted_words: consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg

text_blocks.snippet: Readings consist of two numbers: systolic (top number, pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (bottom number, pressure when the heart rests between beats).
Note: A reading above 180/120 mm Hg paired with warning signs—such as chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, or vision changes—requires an immediate 911 call.
